in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

(In the UK, Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age - children under 16 automatically qualify, those aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in education or training, and children aged 20 or over don't qualify.)

Thank you for that information! So I'm helping you with **one child: Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For young people in this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they are in **full-time education or an approved training course**.

**Can you tell me: Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

(This could include things like school, college, university, or an approved vocational training programme.)

## **Result: NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### **Why:**

Child Benefit has specific age and education requirements:
- ✅ Children **under 16** automatically qualify
- ✅ Young people **aged 16-19** can qualify if they're in **full-time education or approved training**
- ⚠️ There's a **20-week extension** after leaving education, but only if the young person registers with a careers service or armed forces
- ❌ Young people **20 or over** don't qualify

**In Alex's situation:**
- He's 18 years old (within the 16-19 range, so potentially eligible)
- However, he's **not in full-time education or training** - he's working full-time instead
- He left school in **June (6 months ago)**, which is **well beyond the 20-week extension period**

### **What happens now:**

Since Alex no longer qualifies, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him. If his circumstances change (for example, if he enrolls in full-time education or training), you could reapply at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding this decision?
